chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Abu Ayyub from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Hamzah from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said:
I asked him about the pledge (rahn) and the guarantor (kafil) in a sale on credit (bai' al-nasi'ah). He said, 'There is no objection to it.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no objection to it / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is using a pledge and guarantor valid in a credit sale according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) validates the use of both a pledge (rahn) and a guarantor (kafil) within a credit sale (bai' al-nasi'ah), clarifying that these security mechanisms do not invalidate the transaction. This ruling underscores the flexibility of Shia commercial jurisprudence in accommodating risk mitigation through multiple layers of assurance, ensuring creditor rights while maintaining the integrity of the sale contract.
